title: Week 1: The Stranger

cards.text: The Goose Union demands a pond. Inside City Hall. In your office, specifically.

options.label: Build the pond
options.reaction: Honk. That means thank you. Probably.

options.label: Pond in the park instead
options.reaction: A compromise. We will remember this. Fondly, for now.

options.label: Refuse
options.reaction: The union will hear of this. They are right behind you.

advisors.line: Geese don't pay taxes. I checked.
The children love the geese. The geese do not love the children.

cards.text: We need a helicopter. For crime. And also, mostly, for fun.

options.label: Buy it
options.reaction: I call the front seat. Forever.

options.label: Lease one
options.reaction: A rental. Fine. I'm still doing the noises.

options.label: Promise it next quarter
options.reaction: I'm writing that down. In pen.

advisors.line: It costs four thousand a month just to look at it.
'Chief Buzzes Town.' I'd print that.

cards.text: The only snowplow is broken. School road or Chad's shopping street? The other stays buried.

options.label: Plow the school road
options.reaction: The children can learn again. Chad is calling. I'm not answering.

options.label: Plow Chad Street
options.reaction: The shops are open. The school is an igloo now.

options.label: Rent a second plow
options.reaction: Two plows. I need to sit down.

advisors.line: The children are sledding to school. On each other.
Snow is bad for business. Unless you sell snow.

cards.text: Put a casino in the library. Books are just slow slot machines.

options.label: Build the casino
options.reaction: You won't regret this. Others will.

options.label: Refuse
options.reaction: Fine. Enjoy your free knowledge.

options.label: Casino night, once a year
options.reaction: One night. I'll make it count.

advisors.line: The books already know who wins.
I'd have to arrest the librarian. Again.

cards.text: The Bugle needs a front page. Can we say you wrestled a bear?

options.label: Yes, I wrestled a bear
options.reaction: Wonderful. Did you win? Never mind, you won.

options.label: Tell the truth
options.reaction: Honesty. On a Tuesday. Bold.

advisors.line: Lying about bears is a crime. I just made that a crime.
Did the bear have a name?

cards.text: Every great town has a giant something. I have drawings of a spoon. Do not ask why a spoon.

options.label: Build the spoon
options.reaction: It faces north. That part matters.

options.label: A normal-sized spoon
options.reaction: You've made a spoon. Congratulations.

options.label: No spoon
options.reaction: That's what they want you to say.

advisors.line: Tourists love a big thing. I'll sell small versions of it.
A spoon. With our money. I feel faint.

cards.text: The school has one textbook. It is about boats. We are not near water.

options.label: Build a new school
options.reaction: The PTA approves. We have never said that before.

options.label: Promise it by spring
options.reaction: Spring. I'll bring a calendar.

options.label: Buy a second book
options.reaction: It's also about boats.

advisors.line: Fifty thousand. I'll be under my desk.
I like the boat book.

cards.text: The Bugle wants a TV station. Print is dying. I'd like to watch it happen in colour.

options.label: Build the station
options.reaction: You're on at six. Wear a tie.

options.label: Lend her the roof
options.reaction: The antenna is mostly safe.

options.label: Refuse
options.reaction: Then tomorrow's headline writes itself.

advisors.line: I'd buy ad time. All of it.
She'll film my parking.

cards.text: We could put parking meters on Main Street. People will hate it. The budget will not.

options.label: Install meters
options.reaction: Coins. Lovely, countable coins.

options.label: Meters for visitors only
options.reaction: How do we know who's a visitor? Never mind.

options.label: Free parking forever
options.reaction: Forever is a long time for a budget.

advisors.line: The PTA parks where it likes.
Free parking means chaos. I've seen it.

cards.text: Teens are standing near the fountain. Just standing. I want a curfew.

options.label: Curfew at 9 pm
options.reaction: Order. Beautiful, quiet order.

options.label: Fund a youth centre
options.reaction: Now they stand indoors. I'll allow it.

options.label: Let them stand
options.reaction: Then I'm standing near them. Menacingly.

advisors.line: They're good kids. Mostly mine.
I want to stand near the fountain too.

cards.text: I'd like a small tax break. Tiny. You'd need a telescope to see it. I own the telescope shop.

options.label: Grant the tax break
options.reaction: A pleasure doing business with the public.

options.label: Trade it for a donation
options.reaction: I love a deal. I'll name a bench after you.

options.label: Refuse
options.reaction: I'll remember this at the country club.

advisors.line: We can't afford tiny.
'Mayor Bends For Billionaire.' Or not. Your call.

cards.text: Can the town have a Frog Day? I already told everyone there's a Frog Day.

options.label: Fund Frog Day
options.reaction: FROG DAY! FROG DAY!

options.label: Promise Frog Day soon
options.reaction: How many sleeps is soon?

options.label: No Frog Day
options.reaction: I'm telling the frogs.

advisors.line: Honk. (He is against frogs.)
Frogs block traffic. Slowly, but they do.

cards.text: Main Street has a pothole so big it has a name. The name is Kevin.

options.label: Fill in Kevin
options.reaction: Goodbye, Kevin. You were expensive.

options.label: Sell tickets to see Kevin
options.reaction: People are queuing. To look at a hole.

options.label: Leave Kevin alone
options.reaction: Kevin is growing.

advisors.line: Kevin ate my car. I have other cars, but still.
Kevin has more readers than you.

cards.text: I'm giving the town a statue. Of me. It's forty feet tall and it winks.

options.label: Accept the statue
options.reaction: It winks at night too. You'll get used to it.

options.label: A statue of someone normal
options.reaction: Who's Brenda? Why does Brenda get a statue?

options.label: No statues
options.reaction: I'll put it just outside town. Facing in.

advisors.line: The children are scared of the wink.
Statues are how they watch us.

cards.text: Raccoons are getting into the bins. They're organised. I think they have a leader.

options.label: Raccoon-proof bins
options.reaction: Let's see them open THAT. Oh. They opened it.

options.label: Night patrols
options.reaction: We patrol all night. People complain about the torches.

options.label: They live here too
options.reaction: You're soft on raccoons. Suspiciously soft.

advisors.line: We... I mean I... think bins should be free. For everyone.
Bins cost money. Everything costs money.

cards.text: The Bugle's printing press exploded. A little. The town could buy us a new one.

options.label: Buy a new press
options.reaction: Tomorrow's edition will be very kind to you.

options.label: Use the school copier
options.reaction: The paper smells like homework now.

options.label: Not the town's problem
options.reaction: I'll write tomorrow's paper by hand. About you.

advisors.line: That copier is for bake sale flyers.
I could buy the Bugle. Just saying.

cards.text: School lunch is beige. All of it. The children have started calling it 'the paste'.

options.label: Pay for real food
options.reaction: A vegetable! Some of them cried.

options.label: Chad sponsors lunch
options.reaction: 'Chad Nuggets.' The Bugle is having a field day.

options.label: Paste builds character
options.reaction: The PTA has a long memory.

advisors.line: The paste is okay if you don't look.
I tried the paste. I'm suing.

cards.text: It's my birthday. Can the whole town have fireworks? I told the whole town yes.

options.label: Fireworks for Timmy
options.reaction: BEST. MAYOR. EVER.

options.label: One sparkler
options.reaction: It's... one. It's a small one.

options.label: No fireworks
options.reaction: I'm un-inviting you.

advisors.line: Fireworks are just crime in the sky.
HONK. (Geese hate fireworks.)

cards.text: I need a weather radar. Right now I lick my finger and guess.

options.label: Buy the radar
options.reaction: I can see rain coming! It's... already raining.

options.label: Promise it next quarter
options.reaction: I'll keep licking the finger till then.

options.label: The finger is fine
options.reaction: Then tomorrow will be... weather.

advisors.line: Twenty thousand to know it's raining.
His guesses fill half my paper.

cards.text: Open the library at night. The best books only talk after dark.

options.label: Fund the night library
options.reaction: Shh. They're starting.

options.label: Let her run a 'truth club'
options.reaction: We meet Tuesdays. Bring string.

options.label: Libraries close at five
options.reaction: That's what the daytime books want.

advisors.line: Nothing good happens in a library at night.
Can I come? I'm allowed up till eight.

cards.text: I'd like to pave the park. For parking. Think of it as a very flat park.

options.label: Pave the park
options.reaction: Smell that? Asphalt. Progress.

options.label: Only half the park
options.reaction: Half a park. Half a car park. Everyone's half happy.

options.label: Hands off the park
options.reaction: Trees don't shop, you know.

advisors.line: HONK. (The pond is in the park.)
Touch that park and the PTA mobilises.

cards.text: Let me hide behind the 'Welcome' sign with a radar gun. Visitors drive so fast.

options.label: Approve the speed trap
options.reaction: Seventeen tickets before lunch. A good day.

options.label: Warning signs only
options.reaction: A sign. They'll just read it and slow down. Boring.

options.label: No speed trap
options.reaction: Then I'm hiding there anyway. For fun.

advisors.line: You're ticketing my customers.
Twelve thousand, though.

cards.text: The town needs a mascot. Our readers voted. They chose 'Wet Sock'.

options.label: Welcome, Wet Sock
options.reaction: He's damp. He's proud. He's ours.

options.label: Hire a real designer
options.reaction: A smiling building. Readers call it 'Dry Sock'.

options.label: No mascot
options.reaction: You can't cancel Wet Sock. He's already at the school.

advisors.line: I can't put a wet sock on a billboard.
I LOVE WET SOCK.

cards.text: The geese are on strike. Nobody is eating the bugs. The bugs have noticed.

options.label: Meet their demands
options.reaction: Honk. (Work resumes.)

options.label: Hire ducks instead
options.reaction: Ducks. You hired DUCKS.

options.label: Wait them out
options.reaction: The bugs are forming their own union.

advisors.line: I can't arrest a goose. I've asked.
Cloudy, with mosquitoes.

cards.text: I found $30k extra in the budget. It's Chad's. The bank made a mistake. Nobody knows.

options.label: Keep it quiet
options.reaction: I'm going to be sick. Rich, but sick.

options.label: Give it back
options.reaction: Chad says thanks. He didn't notice it was gone.

options.label: Split it with Chad
options.reaction: A finder's fee. He respects that.

advisors.line: If I find out, that's a front page.
The school roof costs exactly thirty thousand.

cards.text: Lovely town. How much for all of it? I'm asking for a friend. The friend is me.

options.label: Name a silly price
options.reaction: A billion and a goose. Interesting. I'll be back.

options.label: Throw him out
options.reaction: I've been thrown out of better towns. This one, actually.

options.label: Hear him out
options.reaction: A deposit. No strings. Well, a few strings.

advisors.line: I know that walk. I just can't place it.
Hey, I was going to buy the town.

cards.text: The PTA talent show needs a judge. It's you. Every child sings the same song.

options.label: Judge honestly
options.reaction: 'Mayor Makes Children Cry.' Front page.

options.label: Everyone wins
options.reaction: Forty trophies. You're paying for forty trophies.

options.label: Send Dave
options.reaction: Dave ate a trophy. The kids loved it.

advisors.line: I'm doing the song. But louder.
Please be honest. I need this.

cards.text: Farmers are selling carrots in my car park. Carrots! For less than my carrots!

options.label: Protect the market
options.reaction: Enjoy your cheap carrots. I hope they're crunchy.

options.label: Ban the market
options.reaction: Thank you. Carrots are back to full price.

options.label: Market pays a fee
options.reaction: A carrot tax. I can live with that.

advisors.line: Those farmers are PTA dads.
A fee! Finally, some money coming in.

cards.text: The station needs a police dog. We have one. He is scared of crime.

options.label: Buy a braver dog
options.reaction: This one bit me. Perfect.

options.label: Therapy for the old dog
options.reaction: He's talking about his feelings. Well, barking.

options.label: One scared dog is plenty
options.reaction: He hid under my desk when you said that.

advisors.line: Can I pet him? Either him.
Dog therapy. In the budget. Under 'D'.

cards.text: Can the park have wifi? It's for homework. And for one game. Mostly the game.

options.label: Free park wifi
options.reaction: The password is 'frogday'.

options.label: Wifi with Chad's ads
options.reaction: It plays an ad every time you blink.

options.label: Go outside and play
options.reaction: We ARE outside.

advisors.line: I sell wifi. Why is it free?
Wifi is how the pigeons report back.

cards.text: The City Hall basement is haunted. Or it has raccoons. Either way, I want to investigate.

options.label: Fund the ghost hunt
options.reaction: We found a cold spot. And a sandwich.

options.label: Seal the basement
options.reaction: You've sealed it. It knows you sealed it.

options.label: There's nothing down there
options.reaction: That's exactly what something down there would say.

advisors.line: Don't go in the basement. No reason. Just don't.
Ghosts sell papers.

cards.text: A heatwave is coming. Or a cold snap. It's one of those. The pool is cracked either way.

options.label: Fix the pool
options.reaction: It's snowing. But the pool looks great.

options.label: Sprinklers on Main Street
options.reaction: The shoppers are soaked. The children are thrilled.

options.label: Tell them to drink water
options.reaction: Hot, with a chance of angry.

advisors.line: Wet customers don't buy shoes.
The pool is where the PTA plots.

cards.text: The bridge inspector says the bridge is 'mostly fine'. He wouldn't walk on it.

options.label: Repair the bridge
options.reaction: It doesn't wobble. I miss the wobble, a bit.

options.label: Promise repairs soon
options.reaction: Soon. I'll tell the bridge.

options.label: Put up a 'Good Luck' sign
options.reaction: The sign is very popular. The bridge is not.

advisors.line: I'm not driving the helicopter under it. Again.
'Bridge Fine, Says Man Running Away.'

cards.text: I want a billboard on City Hall. Just my face. And the words 'TRUST CHAD'.

options.label: Allow the billboard
options.reaction: It lights up. You'll never need a lamp again.

options.label: A small one, round the back
options.reaction: Nobody can see it. I love it. I hate it.

options.label: No billboard
options.reaction: Then where do people look to trust me?

advisors.line: That's MY job. Putting faces on things.
It blinks in code.

cards.text: The school needs a crossing guard. The only volunteer is Gerald.

options.label: Hire a human
options.reaction: He has a little sign and everything.

options.label: Gerald it is
options.reaction: Traffic has stopped. All of it. For hours.

options.label: Children can look both ways
options.reaction: I'm putting that on a banner. With your name.

advisors.line: A goose cannot direct traffic. He has tried.
Honk. (He says he's qualified.)

cards.text: A rival paper has started: The Whistle. Shut it down and The Bugle will adore you.

options.label: Shut down The Whistle
options.reaction: One paper. One voice. Mine.

options.label: Buy The Whistle
options.reaction: You own a newspaper now. It's mostly recipes.

options.label: A free press is good
options.reaction: Then read what The Whistle says about your hair.

advisors.line: The Whistle prints the real weather.
Two papers means two ad bills.

cards.text: The geese have occupied the parking lot. They have a list of demands. It is mostly honking.

options.label: Pay them off in bread
options.reaction: The bread is acceptable. The parking lot is yours. For now.

options.label: Send Chief Barb
options.reaction: You sent the police. Against geese. Noted.

advisors.line: My car is in there.

cards.text: Someone stole the 'Welcome to Town' sign. And the backup sign. Morale is low at the station.

options.label: Pay for overtime
options.reaction: We'll find that sign. Or a similar sign.

options.label: Blame the next town over
options.reaction: Classic them.

cards.text: Someone is counting cards at the library casino. It's the librarian. She's very good.

options.label: Ban Linda from blackjack
options.reaction: She's moved to roulette. She's good at that too.

options.label: Make her head of security
options.reaction: Nobody cheats now. She can smell it.

cards.text: We love you so much we went through your bins. You eat a LOT of string cheese. It's tomorrow's story.

options.label: Own it
options.reaction: 'Mayor: I Regret Nothing.' Perfect.

options.label: Bury the story
options.reaction: What story? Exactly.

cards.text: The people adore you. So they'd like free ice cream. Every day. They said you'd say yes.

options.label: Free ice cream
options.reaction: They want sprinkles next. I'm just the messenger.

options.label: Say no nicely
options.reaction: They took it badly. One man lay down.

cards.text: Business is so good I'd like to buy the town. Not all of it. Just the parts with roads.

options.label: Sell him Main Street
options.reaction: Welcome to Chad Street. Tolls start Monday.

options.label: Refuse
options.reaction: Everything has a price. I'll wait.

cards.text: With this much support I've started arresting people for jaywalking. And for walking. Thoughts?

options.label: Rein her in
options.reaction: Fine. Walking is legal again.

options.label: Let it ride
options.reaction: The streets have never been emptier.

cards.text: You found the ballots. Fine. I was mayor once. They voted for a goose instead. Help me, or expose me.

options.label: Expose him in The Bugle
options.reaction: Print it. I've been run out of town by worse. By geese.

options.label: Take his hush money
options.reaction: Smart. Wrong, but smart.

cards.text: RARE. A golden goose has landed on City Hall. Gerald says it is his cousin. It lays one egg.

options.label: Sell the egg
options.reaction: HONK. (That was his cousin's egg.)

options.label: Give the egg to the town
options.reaction: The egg has its own parade now.

events.text: It's Founders' Day. The parade float is a papier-mache you. It's on fire. Slightly.

options.label: Ride the float anyway
options.reaction: You waved the whole time. While smoking.

options.label: Buy a new float
options.reaction: The new you has two eyes the same size.

events.text: Stormy Steve predicts 'weather'. He will not say which kind. He looks worried.

options.label: Buy sandbags
options.reaction: Sandbags! Good for most weather. Not all.

options.label: Ignore Steve
options.reaction: That's what the last mayor did.

events.text: Someone slid a note under your door: 'LOOK IN THE BASEMENT.' The handwriting is very neat.

options.label: Go and look
options.reaction: Boxes. Hundreds of boxes. All marked 'DO NOT COUNT'.

options.label: Burn the note
options.reaction: A second note arrives. It says 'RUDE.'

events.text: A bear is in my office. It says you two need to talk.

options.label: Apologise to the bear
options.reaction: The bear accepts. It wants a column.

options.label: Wrestle it for real
options.reaction: You lost. But we got photos.

events.text: The power is out. The town is dark. Chad's mansion is still lit. He has 'a guy'.

options.label: Pay Chad's guy
options.reaction: The lights are on. The bill says 'guy stuff'.

options.label: Hand out candles
options.reaction: Cosy. Also four small fires.

events.text: The basement boxes are old ballots. From the last election. Every single one says 'Gerald'.

options.label: Tell the town
options.reaction: So the goose won. And nobody said.

options.label: Put the boxes back
options.reaction: You saw nothing. The boxes saw you.

events.text: The county fair is here. Timmy entered you in the pie contest. As a pie eater. Against Gerald.

options.label: Eat for the town
options.reaction: Second place. To a goose. Still, a medal!

options.label: Decline politely
options.reaction: Gerald wins by default. He's unbearable about it.

events.text: Tonight: the mayoral debate. Your opponent is a traffic cone. It is polling well.

options.label: Debate with facts
options.reaction: You won on points. The cone won on charm.

options.label: Debate with insults
options.reaction: 'Orange And Empty,' says Mayor. Crowd gasps.

campaign.text: Election day. The town knows a goose won last time. Run on honesty, or run from it?

options.label: 'At least I'm not a goose'
options.reaction: Gerald heard. Gerald is at the window.

options.label: Promise a recount
options.reaction: Brave. If Gerald wins again, we're moving.

options.label: Big rally
options.reaction: We ordered balloons. So many balloons.

options.label: Call in every Favor
options.reaction: Phones are ringing. People owe you.

campaign.text: Election day. One last push. What's the plan, boss? We believe in you. All three of us.

options.label: Big rally
options.reaction: We ordered balloons. So many balloons.

options.label: Call in every Favor
options.reaction: Phones are ringing. People owe you.

options.label: Attack ad about the cone
options.reaction: The cone did not respond. Classic cone.

options.label: Just be yourself
options.reaction: Risky. We love it.

objectives.text: Find out what is in the basement

cliffhangers: Tomorrow: Stormy Steve has a forecast. He's whispering it.
Tomorrow: someone has left you a note. The handwriting is very neat.
Tomorrow: The Bugle has a visitor. A large one.
Tomorrow: the basement. Bring a torch.
Tomorrow: the debate. Your opponent is orange and says nothing.
Tomorrow: the voters decide. Wear the good tie.
recallEndings: The town voted to replace you with a traffic cone. The cone declined. You're Acting Mayor.
You were chased out by a crowd. Then chased back in, because nobody else wanted the job.
The recall passed. The paperwork was eaten by a goose. You're still here, sort of.
The town's wallet is empty. It also has a moth in it. You're Acting Mayor now.

outcomes.text: Dave solved it. Nobody knows how. Dave included.
Dave handled it from inside a bin. It mostly worked.
Dave found $9,000 in a hedge and called it 'the budget'.
Dave traded the problem for something shiny.
Dave hissed at everyone until they left.
Dave gave a press conference. All three of him spoke at once.
Dave fell asleep on the paperwork. The problem got bored and left.
Dave knows a guy. The guy is also a raccoon.
Dave ate the request.
Dave's plan was brilliant. Please stop asking him to explain it.
The trench coat came open mid-meeting. Everyone agreed to say nothing.
Dave washed the paperwork in the fountain. It's very clean now.
Dave stood on his own shoulders and gave a speech. People clapped.
Dave shook hands with Chad. Chad counted his fingers afterwards.
Dave borrowed Chief Barb's badge. She wants it back. And an apology.
Dave gave Marge an exclusive. It was mostly chittering. She printed it.
Dave billed the town for 'lunch'. Lunch was a whole buffet.
Dave signed it with a paw print. Legally, that counts.
Dave fixed it at 3 am. Something is missing from every bin in town.
Dave panicked and split into three. Each one did a third of the job.
Dave threw a gala. In a skip. It was the event of the season.

absence: Dave governed from a shopping trolley.
Dave signed everything. With a paw print.
Dave held office hours at 3 am, behind the diner.
Dave moved the mayor's desk into a bin. He says it's 'more efficient'.

headlines.text: Geese Get Pond, Demand Second Pond
Chief Barb Airborne, Refuses To Land
Library Now Has Blackjack, Still Shushes You
MAYOR WRESTLES BEAR, WINS, SAYS MAYOR
New School Opens, Has Two Books
Town Gets TV Station; Marge Gets Worse
Mayor's Promise Found Broken Behind Shed
Mayor Keeps Promise; Town Checks For Catch
Two Bad Ideas Combine Into One Good One
Mayor Makes Decision; Experts Unsure Which
MAYOR RECALLED, THEN UN-RECALLED, TOWN TIRED
